evidence: Receiving DO2 collapse at 46.2h: 12.2 -> 3.7 mg/L, then to ~1.7-2.4 mg/L through 52h
Receiving P(48h)=2.33 g/L vs source-1/2/3 at 48h: 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L (~25% deficit)
Source DO2 dips (e.g. ~24h in source-1) recover by 28h; receiving dip persists to 52h - not a normal transient
Source trajectories show DO2 floor of ~7.4-9 mg/L at comparable late times; receiving is far outside that envelope
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~46 h from ~12 mg/L to below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen floor (readings 1.67-1.96 at 50-52 h), indicating oxygen demand exceeding transfer capacity in the receiving vessel. A KEEP would leave an active constraint violation. Combined intervention (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) attacks both sides of the oxygen balance with a bounded, reversible action: it restores DO2 margin above the floor while retaining 80% of feed and all accumulated product mass. Increase_air alone (15%) may be insufficient given the depth of the collapse; strong_feed_reduction sacrifices disproportionate production for margin we likely do not need; stop yields zero counted production. No extra assay requested because the 4 h turnaround delays action while the process sits at/below the DO floor under KEEP.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters (kLa, biomass, substrate) are unobservable; magnitude of demand reduction from a 20% feed cut is estimated, not measured. If demand is driven mainly by high biomass rather than feed, combined may under-deliver and strong_feed_reduction would be the fallback; if transfer capacity is nearly adequate, increase_air alone would have sufficed and combined costs some feed-driven production. The receiving assay history is limited to 4 h lags, so product benefit is only indirectly estimated from the source trajectories.
